results.note: When focus is inside the command line input, isTextEntry() returns true so the global keydown bridge does NOT intercept; the CommandLine owns Enter and submits the line, which the engine echoes as 'tenmol>...'. Affirmative proof the gate lets text fields keep their keys.

Real keydowns for 'z','q','j' into the focused command line must land in the input (the bridge must not preventDefault them). Submitting echoes 'tenmol>zqj'. If the gate were broken, the letters would be intercepted/preventDefaulted and the echo would be empty -> feedbackMatches fails.
